documents.title: Detroit DDC-SVC-BRO-0115 controller and emissions-generation fault catalog
documents.summary: The supplied Detroit reference is a 71-page SPN/FMI catalog spanning GHG14 ACM2.1, CPC4 and MCM2.1 plus EPA10 ACM/MCM/CPC and EPA07 CPC/MCM. Panta must identify both controller/generation and exact SPN/FMI because the same SPN can have different descriptions by module and FMI.

documents.title: GHG14 ACM2.1 aftertreatment fault families
documents.summary: GHG14 ACM2.1 catalog covers CAN signal availability, battery voltage, DEF level/temperature, inlet and outlet NOx sensors, DOC/DPF temperatures and pressures, DEF dosing valve and pump, DEF quality, sensor supplies, parked regeneration failures, soot/ash conditions, SCR line heaters, SCR conversion efficiency, DEF pressure/control and regulatory derates. Examples include SPN 625 CPC/PT-CAN communication, 1761 DEF level, 3031 DEF temperature, 3216/3226 NOx sensors, 3251 DPF pressure, 3364 improper DEF quality, 3719 soot level, 4334 DEF pressure sensor, 4364 SCR efficiency, 4374 DEF pressure control and 5246 regulatory derate.

documents.title: GHG14 CPC4 vehicle-side fault families
documents.summary: GHG14 CPC4 catalog covers park brake, vehicle speed, accelerator pedal, engine protection broadcasts, battery/power, transmission and cruise messages, CPC hardware/software, J1708/J1939/PT-CAN, digital/analog inputs and outputs, remote accelerator, PTO, ABS/wheel-speed messages, optimized idle, regeneration switches and automatic gear-selection/ITPM faults. Important families include SPN 91 and 2623 accelerator channels, 168 power, 247 engine-hours data, 609 CPC hardware/software/temperature, 625 network/module messages, 628 EEPROM, 629 CPC mismatch/Xflash, 639 J1939, 3510 pedal supply and 524286 automatic gear-selection faults.

documents.title: GHG14 MCM2.1 engine-management fault families
documents.summary: GHG14 MCM2.1 catalog covers intake throttle, vehicle speed, low-side fuel pressure, water-in-fuel, oil pressure, boost/turbo, coolant, high-pressure fuel rail, oil/fuel temperature, EGR delta pressure/flow/actuator, MCM-ACM communication, crank/cam sensors, injectors cylinders 1-6, starter relay, fan/Jake brake outputs, quantity-control valve and leak-down faults, misfire/idle smoothness, charge-air cooler, HC doser, sensor supplies and injector amplifier/spill-control circuits.

documents.title: EPA10 ACM aftertreatment fault families
documents.summary: EPA10 ACM catalog covers aftertreatment controller power/internal errors, CAN-broadcast inputs, DEF level and dosing hardware, NOx/SCR, DOC/DPF temperature and pressure, regeneration and emissions-protection conditions. Use EPA10-specific SPN/FMI descriptions rather than assuming GHG14 wording.

documents.title: EPA10 MCM engine fault families
documents.summary: EPA10 MCM catalog covers intake throttle, vehicle speed, fuel supply and rail pressure, water-in-fuel, oil/coolant temperatures and pressure, EGR, engine CAN/ACM communication, crank/cam sensing, injector circuits, starter relay, fan/Jake brake, quantity-control valve, charge-air cooler and other engine-management faults. Exact EPA10 SPN/FMI should control interpretation.

documents.title: EPA10 CPC vehicle-interface fault families
documents.summary: EPA10 CPC catalog covers coolant-level broadcasts, ignition/power, battery, ambient temperature, transmission output/current gear, cruise and retarder messages, accelerator/idle validation, J1939/J1708 communication and CPC input/output functions. Diagnose network and power faults before condemning a controller.

documents.title: EPA07 CPC and MCM fault families
documents.summary: EPA07 sections provide separate CPC and MCM SPN/FMI catalogs for earlier Detroit electronic systems. Keep EPA07 results isolated from EPA10/GHG14 when answering because controller architecture, descriptions and diagnostic meaning can differ by emissions generation.

documents.title: Detroit fault-code interpretation rule
documents.summary: Always use the complete SPN + FMI + reporting controller + emissions generation. A fault description reports a detected condition and does not prove the named sensor, actuator or ECU is defective. Correlate companion faults, power/grounds, wiring/connectors, CAN/J1939 communication, programming/configuration and applicable Detroit troubleshooting before recommending replacement.
